reasoning_traces.think:
The primitives emerge from dual experimental frameworks: one focusing on sign-gestalt expectation formation (e.g., spider web behavior), and another on docile fright adaptation (e.g., Jones’ rabbit experiment). These are unified mathematically through conditional behavioral modulation, which acts as a kernel linking perception to action. The core operator is a stochastic process where expectation E_s evolves over time T, modulated by external stimuli S_t and internal reward/punishment signals R_i. In the spider case, staying on the web leads to injury (negative outcome), whereas dropping off allows escape (positive outcome). This creates a binary decision boundary governed by a probabilistic threshold. For the child-rabbit paradigm, fear diminishes through repeated exposure and reward pairing (feeding), indicating a dynamic adjustment of F_d. Both cases converge on a shared structure: a feedback loop between stimulus, expectation, and behavioral change. The failure mode arises when expectations become misaligned with actual outcomes, leading to maladaptive responses. Dual experiments provide empirical validation by testing both sides of the behavioral spectrum.
